signal: Calculate refill interval variance and flag near-deterministic shipment schedules over six or more cycles.
Flag refills with no documented beneficiary/caregiver request within the required pre-dispensing window.
Flag shipments after death, hospice election, institutional admission, therapy discontinuation, or equipment return.
Compare billed quantity and days' supply with prior utilization, remaining inventory, and early-refill history.
Measure beneficiary complaint, return-to-supplier, unopened-package, and reversal rates by supplier and marketer.
For each supplier, calculate the percentage of refill claims preceded by a documented beneficiary/caregiver request within a defined operational window; flag rates below the plan benchmark.

Calculate ordering-provider and marketer-linked beneficiary concentration using Herfindahl-Hirschman Index; flag suppliers where the top 5 ordering providers account for more than 50% of recurring-supply beneficiaries or where one provider is shared across multiple suppliers.
Flag refill intervals with coefficient of variation below 0.10 across at least four cycles when beneficiary-request timestamps are absent or identical across many beneficiaries.
Flag beneficiaries receiving the same supply category from multiple network suppliers within the same expected replacement interval.
Compare billed units with prior utilization, documented DME ownership, and days since last shipment; flag repeated claims at or near frequency limits.
Calculate ordering-provider concentration by supplier, HCPCS family, diagnosis, and month; flag top-provider share above 40% or HHI above peer percentile.
Measure template similarity of order narratives, CMNs, or supporting notes; flag high textual similarity across unrelated beneficiaries.
Flag ordering providers whose DMEPOS order volume is extreme relative to their Medicare patient panel, specialty, or evaluation-and-management activity.
Flag short intervals between beneficiary enrollment, telehealth encounter, order signature, and high-volume DMEPOS claim across many beneficiaries.
Compare order diagnoses and equipment combinations with clinical encounters, functional findings, and prior equipment history; flag product-specific diagnosis patterns.
Rate of QG, QF, QB, or high-flow claims by supplier compared with regional peers.
Beneficiary-months with mutually exclusive stationary, portable, and contents payments.
Ownership-status transitions without a corresponding purchase, title, or equipment history event.
Portable oxygen claims within 30 days before or after QG claims despite the stated CWF edit.
Average prescribed flow rates just above modifier thresholds, such as greater than 4 LPM, by ordering provider.
Beneficiary-equipment episodes with more than 15 paid rental months absent a validated reset.
Number of supplier changes during a single equipment episode.
New KH claims within 12 months of a prior supplier's KJ or month-10/15 claim.
Rental claims with gaps shorter than 60 days but new prescriptions or apparent new episodes.
Anniversary-date changes not supported by an inpatient or SNF stay overlapping the original anniversary date.
For each beneficiary-HCPCS family, construct a continuous rental episode and flag more than 15 paid rental months absent a documented qualifying interruption or managed-care transition.
Flag a new KH or first-month rental modifier within 60 days of the prior supplier's KJ month or final rental claim.
Flag supplier changes where the replacement supplier bills more months than the calculated remaining months in the episode.
Flag overlapping monthly rental claims from different suppliers for the same or similar HCPCS family.
Flag post-cap rental claims lacking evidence of title status, beneficiary ownership, or the applicable maintenance-and-servicing pathway.
Flag supplier claims for nonroutine supply codes during active HHA PPS episodes.
Flag DMEPOS claims during hospice enrollment where the diagnosis is related to the terminal condition or no unrelated-condition documentation exists.
Measure abrupt HCPCS/POS/entity changes within 14 days of HHA admission, discharge, hospice election, or revocation.
Identify duplicate or functionally equivalent supply claims across HHA, hospice, and DME supplier entities.
Compare beneficiary-level DME, supply, oxygen, and plan-of-care utilization before, during, and after institutional episodes.
Flag beneficiaries with a second capped-rental start within 180 days of the last rental or ownership event.
Calculate the gap between the last paid rental month and the new episode; prioritize gaps near the regulatory interruption threshold.
Measure the proportion of new episodes supported by an inpatient stay, HHA episode, voluntary nonbilling period, or supplier change rather than documented clinical resolution.
Flag same-or-similar HCPCS restarts with unchanged beneficiary address, ordering provider, diagnosis, and equipment serial number.
Compare episode-reset frequency and paid months per beneficiary against peer suppliers and specialty benchmarks.
Flag mutually exclusive oxygen payment combinations within the same calendar month.
Calculate frequency of ownership-status changes by beneficiary and supplier, especially changes occurring near month-end or before a higher-paying modifier.
Flag QG/QB/QF claims without corroborating prescribed flow and portable-system status.
Identify portable add-ons or contents fees inconsistent with the oxygen billing chart for the beneficiary's equipment ownership state.
Measure flow-rate and modifier changes within 30 days of a claim and compare with physician-order changes and test dates.
E1399 share of supplier P&O claims compared with specialty peers.
Median allowed amount for E1399 divided by the closest standard L-code allowance.
Duplicate or near-duplicate construction narratives across beneficiaries, measured by text similarity above 0.90.
Custom claims lacking a documented design, fabrication, or labor component.
Percentage of custom claims where billed item features are reused across more than 80% of cases.
Percentage of pump-kit claims lacking a paid pump rental, pump purchase, or documented pump order within 90 days.
Component lines billed separately within 30 days of a kit line, normalized by beneficiary and therapy type.
Beneficiaries whose billed administration method changes more than once in 12 months without a revised certification.
Pump-kit utilization above the 95th supplier percentile after adjustment for therapy duration.
Claims where billed calories or units are inconsistent with the current PEN certification.
Repair or maintenance claims per equipment unit per year by supplier versus peer percentile.
MS claims occurring before the 13-month or applicable post-cap threshold.
RP or RB claims without a same-day or nearby documented equipment failure or repair labor code.
Repeated identical parts at intervals shorter than expected useful life.
Cumulative repair payments exceeding 50% or 75% of comparable replacement cost.
For each beneficiary, intersect supplier claim dates with HHA episode dates and flag nonroutine supply codes billed separately during active episodes.
Calculate the percentage of a supplier's claims linked to beneficiaries of one or a small number of HHAs; flag concentration above peer benchmarks.

Flag abrupt shifts from HHA revenue code 0270 or PPS billing to supplier DME MAC billing immediately before or after episode boundaries without a corresponding change in HCPCS category or clinical need.
Compare HHA plan-of-care diagnoses, ordered items, and supplier claims; flag same-day or next-day duplicate supply categories.
Flag DME-exempt categories whose utilization increases materially only during active HHA episodes and is concentrated among related entities.
Compare each oxygen claim's modifier with the prescribed flow rate, rest/exercise status, daytime/nighttime values, and calculated average; flag mismatches.
Flag QG or QB claims with portable claims in the preceding or following 30 days, including claims split across related suppliers.
Calculate ordering-provider and testing-facility concentration for claims with flow greater than 4 LPM; flag extreme concentration versus peer suppliers.
Flag repeated modifier changes across successive months without a new order, qualifying test, or documented clinical change.
Flag beneficiaries receiving separate stationary and portable equipment claims that conflict with the ownership/rental combinations in the oxygen billing chart.
Quantity per beneficiary, body area, garment type, and rolling 6- or 24-month window.
RA claims occurring before the applicable replacement interval.
Component-plus-global payment ratio by supplier and code family.
Number of distinct body areas billed per beneficiary compared with clinical diagnosis and therapy records.
Supplier-level average allowed amount per lymphedema episode versus national allowed amounts and peers.
Flag upgraded claims without the required two adjacent lines and expected modifier pairing.
Flag GA claims with no ABN record, ABN date after delivery, or beneficiary knowledge inconsistent with assignment status.
Flag purchase-path upgrades where the baseline HCPCS is a rental class.
Calculate supplier-level upgrade rates, beneficiary liability, and concentration by ordering provider.
Flag repeated upgrades for the same beneficiary or ordering provider without changed medical need or new equipment features.
Use change-point analysis to identify material HCPCS or modifier-mix changes within 30, 60, and 90 days after denial, prepayment review, or audit notification.
For each equipment model or product identifier, calculate the number of HCPCS/modifier pathways used; flag high pathway diversity relative to peers.
Flag claims where line 1 and line 2 do not satisfy the required adjacent upgraded-item structure, or where GA/GZ/GK usage changes without corresponding ABN evidence.
Flag E1399 claims following denials of a specific coded item when make/model, ordering provider, beneficiary, and clinical indication remain materially unchanged.
Compare code-path changes across related suppliers and consultants; flag synchronized changes after a common edit or policy update.
Aggregate claims by beneficiary, equipment family, body area, and network rather than by NPI; flag cumulative quantities exceeding section-specific limits or peer distributions.
Calculate time from original delivery to replacement and compare with useful-lifetime, six-month, two-year, or eight-year rules where applicable.
Flag repeated repair-part claims within 90 days of a replacement or purchase claim, and repeated repairs whose cumulative allowed amount approaches or exceeds replacement cost.
Flag lymphedema claims exceeding three daytime or two nighttime items per body area, or replacements earlier than six months or two years without documented exception.
Flag low-frequency patterns such as one accessory or repair every few months that become anomalous over 24-36 months.
Rate of supplier DMEPOS claims during active HH PPS episodes compared with peer suppliers: flag rates above the 95th percentile.
Percentage of supplier beneficiaries with overlapping HHA episodes and the same or related diagnosis within 7 days: flag above 50%.
Supplier claims for codes listed as HH nonroutine supplies during HH episodes, with paid amount greater than zero.
Same-beneficiary HHA and supplier claims for the same HCPCS family within 1, 3, and 7 days.
Change-point analysis showing increased supplier billing after an HHA referral, ownership, or contracting change.
Calculate the percentage of capped-rental claims with a from date equal to an inpatient or SNF discharge date.
Flag full-month payments where home days on the anniversary date are supported only by same-day discharge and no home-delivery or possession evidence exists.
Measure claim resubmission and date-change rates within 30 days of inpatient or SNF denials.
Flag suppliers with unusually high proportions of anniversary-date changes, discharge-date claims, or paid claims immediately following institutional stays.
Compare rental-month sequence and KH/KI/KJ modifiers before and after every anniversary-date reset.
Flag MS/RP/RB claims during active rental periods except explicitly payable capped-rental maintenance circumstances.
Flag maintenance claims during inpatient or SNF stays and compare with equipment possession and facility responsibility.
Calculate repair and maintenance frequency per equipment-month and supplier-level outlier rates.
Identify same-day or near-day rental plus MS/RP/RB combinations for the same HCPCS or serial number.
Flag maintenance payments within warranty periods or without documented labor, part, and incident records.
Calculate elapsed time from verified delivery of the prior item to each replacement claim and flag intervals below the MAC-established useful lifetime.
Flag same-or-similar HCPCS replacements within 60 months absent documented loss, irreparable damage, or substantial clinical change.
Identify replacements where the prior item has active rental payments or ownership status and no retrieval, destruction, theft, or damage record.
Compare replacement rates by supplier, ordering provider, beneficiary cohort, and HCPCS against peer distributions.
Flag replacement claims with changed supplier but unchanged serial number, address, diagnosis, and equipment configuration.
Flag new 15-month pump episodes following exactly two or three months without pump claims but with ongoing PEN nutrients, supplies, HHA visits, or nutrition-related diagnoses.
Flag therapy-type changes unsupported by a revised certification, new physician order, or clinical event.
Identify pump rentals beyond 15 cumulative months by beneficiary and equipment family across suppliers.
Compare pump, nutrient, kit, and certification timelines for gaps and inconsistent therapy states.
Flag supplier changes that coincide with the apparent break but show continuous equipment possession or unchanged delivery location.
Claims with service dates 1-2 days before inpatient discharge.
Percentage of pre-discharge claims lacking a qualified home-like discharge destination.
Delivery address mismatch between claim, supplier proof of delivery, and beneficiary residence.
Rental first-month claims with a date earlier than discharge or actual home delivery.
Multiple delivery or fitting events from different suppliers within 3 days of discharge.
Flag DME/P&O claims with service dates one or two days before discharge.
Flag claims where the billed date is earlier than both discharge and verified home delivery.
Calculate duplicate or near-duplicate HCPCS/serial-number claims within 14 days of discharge across facility and supplier bill types.
Flag pre-discharge claims with no discharge to home-like POS within two days.
Measure separate delivery-charge frequency on pre-discharge cases and compare with peers.
Calculate the proportion of a supplier's claims routed to each MAC and compare with expected jurisdiction based on supplier location, beneficiary residence, HCPCS, and provider type.
Flag economically similar HCPCS families where the same network bills different entities or claim formats within 30 days for comparable beneficiaries.
Flag supplier-to-beneficiary delivery distances above the 99th percentile, especially when local suppliers exist and separate delivery charges are claimed.
Flag abrupt increases in claims for codes newly assigned to A/B MAC jurisdiction or changes in billing entity immediately after a denial or edit.
Compare paid amounts and denial rates for the same HCPCS family across related entities and jurisdictions; flag material divergence unexplained by beneficiary residence.
Count anniversary-date resets per beneficiary-HCPCS episode and flag more than one reset within 12 months.
Flag claims whose from date equals discharge date but whose delivery, possession, or home-use evidence is absent or occurs later.
Flag full-month rental claims where the beneficiary was inpatient or in an SNF for more than 80% of the month, even if home on the from date.
Flag sequential claims where the new anniversary date is not the documented discharge date after an overlapping stay.
Compare supplier-change dates with discharge dates; flag changes within plus or minus 3 days when the replacement supplier bills an initial or early-month rental modifier.
For each beneficiary-pump combination, count paid rental months across all suppliers and flag totals above 15 absent documented qualifying breaks.
Flag new pump rental periods beginning within 90 days of the prior rental end without two consecutive months showing no medically required PEN services.
Flag therapy-type changes within 60 days of month 12 or 15 of rental, especially when ordering provider, supplier, and diagnosis remain unchanged.
Flag pump purchase or replacement claims occurring near the rental cap without documented purchase date, eight-year ownership history, or revised clinical need.
Flag supply claims during purported two-month medical-need breaks or before the certification and therapy onset dates.
Percentage of supplier claims with service dates within 0-2 days of SNF admission or discharge.
Paid supplier claims whose delivery date falls during an inpatient or SNF stay, excluding validated pre-discharge fitting rules.
Same HCPCS or clinically similar HCPCS billed by both an institution and supplier within 3 days.
Institutional episodes lacking expected bundled items despite supplier claims for the same beneficiary and diagnosis.
Frequency of supplier claims on the discharge date compared with peer distribution.
Cumulative paid amount by beneficiary-equipment episode compared with purchase fee schedule amount.
Claims with both installment indicators and ordinary rental modifiers in the same episode.
Purchase-after-rental claims lacking prior-rental offsets.
New-equipment claims where the item or serial number was previously rented, purchased, or used for another beneficiary.
Supplier-specific rates of BP, BR, BU, NR, NU, RR, and UE combinations inconsistent with peers.
